structure.disclaimer: STRUCTURAL INTENT ONLY - NOT ENGINEERED. Display proxies are not member sizes. Clear-span living/parking is unproven; an engineer may require internal supports or a different layout.
review: Approximately 49.5 ft transverse proxies are not engineered or priced.
Foundations, retaining structure, garden and pool loads, headroom, lift product/pit/overrun and all wind/seismic/fire/structural questions require specialists.

driveway.scope: Sampled low-speed design-vehicle geometry only; street approach, traction, drainage, structures and legal compliance are not certified

weather_protection.status: Open-sided weather shelter, not flood proofing or windblown-dust exclusion. Drainage, sump backup, wind, fire, ventilation and lift/structural design require specialists.

exterior.status: Presentation-only concept facade; materials, window products, glazing performance, roof edge, drainage, lighting and planting are not designed or approved.

review_items: Study 013 adds a 2 x 2 ft single high-sill privacy window to the ground common WC and a 5 x 4 ft double privacy window to the master bath. Master bedroom west window becomes a centred 9 x 7 ft three-section sliding window, with the bed against the east wall facing it; both private dressing and dining-zone entrances remain clear. Its 10 ft rear garden slider remains.

Living has a centred 10 x 7 ft three-section sliding east window kept clear of the TV. With user confirmation, the TV and wooden cabinet move to the north privacy wall beyond the family entrance; the sofa faces north and coffee table is repositioned without occupying pantry, prayer, entrance or garden-exit routes. TV size/viewing distance, window controls, glare, curtains and usable furnishing clearances need review.

Child 1 sleeping room and private bath/dressing suite move front-left, mirroring Child 3's west-window/right-headboard arrangement. Office moves front-right with its front balcony slider but loses side glazing, as confirmed by the user; no exterior window is cut through stairs or the internal gallery. Three child bedrooms remain 16 x 17 ft, office 12 x 17 ft and net family lounge 653 sq ft. Lounge adds a 9 x 7 ft west sliding window and 8 x 7 ft east sliding window, the east span stopping beyond the common WC.

Bathroom windows have high sills and opaque privacy-glass intent, not certified privacy or ventilation performance. Low cutaway models show above-cut-height windows as labelled-intent markers at the wall cap; the finished exterior has their actual heights. Sliding-window sections are presentation intent, not selected products or operable animations. Source extraction, restrictors, fall protection, insect screens, shading and acoustic/thermal/weather performance need design.

Study 012 explicitly expands the illustrative plot to 70 x 116 ft = 8,120 sq ft with user approval, superseding the 7,000 sq ft cap. Whole front/rear yard bands grow from 20/30 ft to 24/42 ft: 1,400 to 1,680 sq ft (+20%) and 2,100 to 2,940 sq ft (+40%). These include paths, terraces, ramp and planting, not grass alone. No actual legal plot or engineering design is approved.

Every Study 011 floor, room, fixture, opening, partition, lift/core and structural row is translated 4 ft rearward with dimensions and elevations unchanged. A 4 ft level ramp approach is added before the old grade profile; the curve, portal and descent stay aligned with the translated basement. Front lawn grows 13 to 17 ft deep; rear play lawn grows 15 to 27 ft. The unchanged-size pool/barrier and rear tree buffer move 16 ft rearward; both veranda decks retain their size.

There is NO external covered stair link and NO extra strip between the main house and driveway. The only above-ground annex is the 60 sq ft front-lawn shaft reserve. Internal Front Galleries meet full-floor front stair landings; the lift never opens at a half-turn or through a bedroom.

Main ground/first plates return to 50 x 50 ft = 2,500 sq ft, plus a 60 sq ft front lift annex each. The basement retains its clean-front / garage-rear arrangement, widened to 50 ft for alignment rather than reverted to an old basement design.

Ground is proposed 1.5 ft above road, basement -8.5 ft, first +12.5 ft and roof +23.5 ft. Basement-to-ground rise stays 10 ft. The slightly raised house helps the sampled ramp roof clearance; entry steps, drainage, accessible arrival and legal levels require design.

Entrance Gallery is reduced from 6 to 4 ft and House Gallery from 5 to 4 ft. Guest grows to 11.5 x 17 ft gross / 157 sq ft net after its ensuite. Master sleeping remains 365.5 sq ft; dressing remains 85.5 sq ft and the left-side bath grows to 102 sq ft. Access is dining/kitchen family zone to bedroom to dressing to bathroom, never public passage through dressing. Modeled openings do not establish finished clear widths.

All three child sleeping rooms remain 16 x 17 ft = 272 sq ft. Office remains 12 x 17 ft / 204 sq ft, with Child 1 bath/dressing in the front band. Unified family lounge is 49 x 14 ft gross minus the 33 sq ft stair-side shared WC = 653 sq ft net. WC is reduced to 6 x 5.5 ft, retaining a basin, wall-backed toilet, 3 ft modeled opening and clear inside approach. East/west galleries remain removed; front stair and rear balcony routes remain 4 ft and open to lounge.

Basement gym and gaming are 387.75 sq ft net EACH. The shaft corner is subtracted from gaming, not double-counted. Existing equipment and recreation functions remain; simultaneous operating/play clearances and six-month storage capacity need review.

Family living is 391.5 gross minus only the 48 sq ft pantry = 343.5 net, including open prayer/circulation. The cupboard no longer occupies living. Dining is 156 sq ft with eight chair footprints, including the 6 sq ft strip that serves the master door; kitchen is 168 sq ft. The master bath is extended to 12 x 8.5 ft = 102 sq ft with one wall-backed WC, one basin, a 4 x 4 ft shower and a 5.5 ft tub. Areas are not added twice; service and operating clearances need review.

All five beds have headboards against solid walls and two bedside tables/lamps. Master has one wall-backed WC, one basin, bathtub and separate shower. Guest ensuite is 5.5 x 7 ft with a 3 x 3 ft enclosed shower; pocket-door operation and all plumbing/accessibility need review.

The separate master entry remains removed. The master bedroom has one 3 ft door in the south end of its east wall, opening to the dining/kitchen family zone, not the House Gallery. The bed headboard is now on the east wall facing the centred 9 ft west sliding window; the 10 ft rear garden slider remains. Door noise, kitchen smell, acoustic/visual privacy and swing/hinge direction need review.

Public gallery/dining screens and an offset 6.5 ft doorless entry protect the family suite. Living, dining and kitchen share open routes, not internal doors. Sampled entrance sightlines are checked against full-height wall intent, not the low display cutaway; all-position privacy/acoustics are not certified.

The user approved a 4 ft long x 2 ft deep cupboard at the right terminal end of House Gallery, facing left into the gallery between stairs and living. It is not a child of living and occupies no living floor. Gallery through-route remains 4 ft, ending at the cupboard's sliding front rather than narrowing beside it. Refrigerator stays in pantry. Storage capacity, door operation, ventilation and child safety need review.

Three SUV bays are at the front of the GARAGE compartment only. A rear arrival aisle and widened 24 ft portal serve the tangent curve. Sampled 5.25 x 2.25 x 2.2 m body/overhang sweep plus 0.3 m buffer, eased grades, roof and underside margins are checked. Independent bay exit/reversing, mirror clearance, road approach, dynamics and engineering remain unverified.

Driveway straight lane is 12 ft, widening to 15 ft around a 19 ft rear-axle radius. Candidate maximum grades are 14% straight and 10% curved. No legal-grade, flood, retaining-wall, slip-resistance or drainage certification is implied.

The garage remains separated by intended sealed full-height construction, two self-closing airlock doors and protected clean routes. Independent exhaust/makeup air, negative pressure, CO/NO2 monitoring, fire/egress and commissioning are unresolved.
Garage and kitchen exhaust outlets are UNLOCATED and must avoid windows, play lawn/veranda, neighbouring land and fresh-air intakes. A window or fan location is not proof of air quality.

The 8 x 16 ft rear-right pool is restored outside the basement footprint and driveway. Its enclosure/gate is modeled, not child-safety certified. Pool structure, excavation separation, drainage, waterproofing and servicing need engineering. Fishpond and double-height atrium remain deferred.

Front/back bands are 24 / 42 ft deep, approximately 20.69% / 36.21% of the expanded plot, with a 50 x 17 ft front lawn and 48 x 27 ft rear play lawn. Ramp/path areas are not play lawn. The raised rear grade, fill/retaining, basement deck, soil depth, roots and drainage need engineering; no mature mini-forest is established.

Roof stair headhouse, front lift-head display reserve and open-sided ramp canopy are separate inspection geometry. Covers reduce rain/sun exposure, not flooding or windblown dust. Inlet/interceptor drains, sump/backup pumps, waterproofing, wind, ventilation and fire require specialists.

The 9 x 17 ft front-entry U-stair retains 4 ft flights/landings, 12 in goings and twenty risers; actual slab voids follow its direction. Headroom, handrail/guard projections, lift product/pit/overrun and code/fire/accessibility remain unverified. Lift is not evacuation egress.

Shared balconies have no internal dividers. The front deck ends before the shaft and has a shared gallery door; rear common access is retained. Guards, insect screens, privacy/shading and daylight/fresh-air performance need detailed design.

Structural view is a non-engineered proxy diagram, not member sizes or a proven load path. Roughly 49.5 ft spans remain substantial; an engineer may require internal columns, transfer systems or layout/budget changes.

No site is purchased. Setbacks, legal plot/buildable envelope, road, neighbours, jurisdiction, groundwater/soil, structural/seismic design, service equipment/LPG/batteries and cost remain unresolved. A geometry PASS is not construction approval.
